segments.text: In childhood, all of us have definitely dreamed of becoming a scientist at some point of time. You may
not know the names of the inventors of mobile phone or computer, but you would definitely know the names of Albert Einstein and
Newton, whereas these people did not invent
any popular everyday use thing but
did deep research in complex subjects like Theoretical Physics Astronomy. If I ask you the name of the best scientist of India,
then you would be Ramanujan, Homi Bhaba, CV Raman. Take the names of Sarabhai and APJ Abdul Kalam ji,
all these scientists also
did deep research in subjects like Physics, Mathematics, Nuclear Science and because of that, their names are known all over the world,
but today the situation in India is that people are not interested in doing even PhD, leave deep research.
On top of that, there is so little support in our country on RAD that
even those who want to do it, leave it midway. Just a few days ago, the budget came in
which the government has given a boost to research and development. Allocate ₹ 000 crore for development, which
is three times more than the normal budget because normally
only 78,000 crore is allocated to the Science Ministry. Our politicians
are also talking a lot about AI. Now even ₹ 10,000 crore has been allocated for AI development. But if
we look at the ground reality, the situation looks quite different. India spends
even 1% of its GDP on AI. India does not spend on research and development and this is the reason why research
students do not even get the necessary equipment. Many students
arrange for the equipment by spending money from their own pockets. The stipend
remains stuck for months and even after getting a PhD, many people
have to apply for peon jobs because there is no guarantee of job and there is no job in core research.
This is the reason why India does not have even a single global Mobile phone
is not a car or appliance maker's company. Even today we
have to use Korean, Japanese, Chinese and European and US products. The blame for this goes to the government but
do you know that our private sector is also responsible for this. India's
big companies are engaged in breaking records and making profits but
do not contribute even 35% on research and development whereas China, Japan, Korea and America
's private sector. Contribution is up to 70% of the total research and development,
that is, if in a year
₹ 100 is spent on research and development by the government and private sector together, then only the private sector spends ₹ 70
there, but the private companies of India are contributing only ₹ 35 and
due to this, our identity in the whole world has remained as a tax supported country.
How difficult is it to do just one PhD in India and why in our country There is no quality
research here. Let's see, if you go to do PhD in India, the biggest
problem is that there are colleges of infrastructure but there are no labs, there
are classrooms but there is no professor. If you find a professor then
he will get all the work done from his office to home to sign your thesis and
the topics for doing PhD are also limited. There are no options for PhD in emerging fields. Many times
consultants cheat in the name of getting admission in big universities by taking money.
Some people even cheat. They buy PhD degree from two tier three colleges and
there is a separate fraud racket going on in it. These fake degrees
are of no use, but just as all the old things change gradually and new things come,
similarly changes are taking place in this too. People did not work in government banks,
then private banks came, super stores were inconvenient, then quick commerce came,
similarly, online DBA has come to solve the problem of PhD. This online
DBA option has been popular in foreign countries for a long time and now through College Vidya, you
can do this course in India too. It is a smarter PhD choice. There
is no consultant or middleman in it. It is an online program, hence no mentor
can make you do household work. It
also has options from human psychology to advanced fields like AIML. It takes 5 to seven years to do offline PhD but
online DBA is only 3 years. These courses are completed in a year. Businessmen also do this
because having the title of Doctor in front of your name also increases your credibility and people
consider you a certified expert in that field. If you are also interested in this,
then there is a link of college education in the description. Do check it out once. Before
talking about PhD, let me explain to you the reality of Research and Development in India.
India spends only around half of its GDP for Research and Development.
If I look at our comparison with other countries, today America allocates
3.5% of its GDP, Germany 3%, China 2.5% and South Korea almost 5%
to research and development. This is India's gross expenditure on RAD. You
must be seeing that it is much less than other countries. On an average, 30 to 40 people
become PhD graduates every year in India. This is the table. Look, in 2021, more than 400 people
had completed PhD in India, 69,000 in USA and 53,000 in China, that is,
we come third in producing PhD holders, but if you
look at the number of researchers in million population, then it is only 262 in India.
You can see for yourself how big a difference there is in comparison to other countries. Apart from this,
look at the number of patents in China. In 2020, almost 8 lakh patents were granted,
more than 3 lakh in the USA and only 3000 in India. These numbers show that because India's
population is so big, you get a lot of PhD holders,
but when you look at the other numbers, the research culture in India is completely exposed.
This chart shows
where the money spent on total research and development in India comes from. In this chart, India is the only one. This is the only country where
the government's share is so high. In India, the government's share is 56%. In USA, it is
only 10%. In India, businesses i.e. private sectors contribute 37%, whereas
in all other countries, the majority contribution comes from business.
In UK, higher education institutions contribute up to 22% on research and development,
whereas in India only 7% What is even more interesting is that
50% of the money that the Government of India spends in research and development every year
goes to only two places i.e. DRDO and ISRO. If we look sector wise, more than 1/3 of
the money is spent in health and defense research. Now this is about finance.
If I talk about infrastructure, there are more than 1000 universities in India,
more than 42,000 colleges and There are more than 11,000 stand alone institutions
but despite this, only 2.7% of the colleges offer PhD programme, only
35% of the colleges are running post graduate programme. In this too, most of the PhD
students are studying in State Public Universities and 23%
in Institutes of Nationality i.e. in colleges like IITs, IIMs, NITS, 14% students
are in Deemed to be Universities and 13% are in Central Universities. Professor D Manjunath of
IIT Bombay, who is doing PhD from universities, had written a paper in which he had claimed that
the applications for PhD in IITs have been continuously falling for the last 10 years.
Students are not preferring to do research in core engineering. He
gave the example of IIT Bombay, where in 2009, a total of 800 applications were received in the field of Electrical Engineer,
which had reached 2150 in 2014, but In 2022,
it has again come down to 900 and similarly in Mechanical Engineering also this year, a total of
300 students applied, which
had increased till 2016 and reached 1450 but in 2022 it has again come down to 950. According to Professor Manjunath, not only
the applications have decreased but
there has also been a huge decline in the quality of applications. According to him, there are three main factors due to which The interest of students
in PhD is falling. The first is
the quality of Masters programs in India. According to them, Jesters are offered in IITs and other technical institutions.
The quality of those programs is very poor
. The second biggest factor is that
by the end of the first semester, not even half the students are left.
Government
Job: He told that in 2010, many PSUs
had started recruitment on the basis of GATE exam, due to which the students who
were interested in PhD have now started preferring to take government job. The third reason
according to them is brain training in STEM field. STEM i.e. Science, Technology,
Engineering and Mathematics. According to The Hindu, in 2010, 400 Indian students were studying
in America in America. And in 2016, this number had gone to 1 lakh and in 2023,
all the records have been broken and this number has gone to 2.5 lakh, that is,
the students of India are now preferring to do Masters and Doctoral programs in India instead of going abroad
and there are many practical reasons for this too. The biggest thing is
the infrastructure which is adequate for PhD students in our Indian colleges.
There is no infrastructure. When I was researching for this video, I
found many stories where these students
have to wait for months just to do an experiment. Students of STEM fields sometimes
need expensive equipments like high end microscope etc. but
in many big colleges, these are not available and even if they are available by mistake, they
are not in working condition. Many times, students have to One has to spend money from one's own pocket and
get their parts from outside because if you ask a college, this whole process
takes months and in some universities even proper labs are not
built. Think for yourself how frustrating it would be for a person
who has chosen a field of research on the basis of his interest. Apart from this, the
major problem that I came to know in my research was the luck of the advisors. If you
get a good advisor then it is fine otherwise. The supervisors or guides who are there
make the life of these PhD students very difficult. I
heard many such stories where students had to leave their PhD midway due to bad supervisors
because these supervisors start using the students as their house servants. Apart from this
, there is very little industry collaboration in most of the PhD programs in India because any student
needs the signature of the supervisor in one of his thesis to
pass his PhD. And to get a signature from him,
he keeps that student as a servant of his house. Apart from this, there
is very little industry collaboration in most of the PhD programs in India, which means that if a
student needs real industry experience, then he
has to figure it out on his own. He does not get much help from the university or supervisor.
Many people also advise that
doing PhD without Junior Research Fellowship is useless. Junior Research Fellowship i.e. JRF. There is a government program
in which after being selected, PhD students
get a monthly stipend of ₹ 37,000 in the first 2 years and if the performance is good then
they are considered as SFR i.e. Senior Research Fellow for the next 3 years and the stipend
increases to ₹ 42,000 per month. But students who have JRF also
say that many times this stipend gets stuck for many months. Due to which
the entire financial burden falls on the student's pocket and this fellowship is also
not available to all the PhD students. There are some criteria which
should be fulfilled in which clearing the NET exam is the most mandatory criteria. Apart from this,
other things are also considered. After that the students are selected and
only a few students are able to avail it. The rest have to bear all
the expenses of PhD from their own pocket. Many people work at the same time at the same time,
but if the supervisor is bad then he can also interfere in this. It
takes 5 to 7 years to complete PhD, that is, it demands a lot of commitment from you and
this time is a very crucial time in the career of any student. Normally a
student graduates from 18 to 21, does master's from 21 to 23 and then
enrolls in a program like PhD, i.e. Between the age of 23 to 28 years,
a lot of financial burden comes on the student. At this age, he
starts feeling shy in even asking for money from his family members. Then,
after seeing other friends who have got jobs and earning money, there is more fear of missing out i.e. FOMO.
Apart from this, pressure of getting married from the family also comes at this time, especially if you
talk about girls and many students do the same, some people
also have children due to which all this happens. It becomes more difficult to manage, that is why
PhD becomes a big mental challenge. Now you must be thinking that
if someone does not have that much time, then why do PhD at all? Mainly,
there are two types of people who do PhD, one who wants to do research in the subject in that field
and the other who want to go to academia i.e. want to do teaching at the college level
because to become an Assistant Professor, one
has to do only Master's degree and clear NET but after that they get promotion.
You might have seen in your college also that many teachers used to do PhD along with teaching,
but there are very few such people because in India there
are more candidates and less jobs, that is why very few people are able to get jobs. Even
more problems are faced by those people who do PhD just for the love of research.
For those people, jobs in India are even less and here a big
fault lies with our private sector. As I told you earlier that
the private sector in our country contributes very less in research and development in comparison to other countries,
that is why research jobs are not created. There are two main reasons for this.
One is that the best talent in the STEM field mostly migrates
to the US and UK. If the companies do not have talent, then who else will innovate?
The risk taking abilities of our private companies are very low. Look at this graph, it is showing
how much Indian companies and global companies of which sector
spend in research and development. From this, you will see Indian companies lagging far behind in every sector.
India has one of the largest software industries in the world, but
despite that, not even 1% is invested in research and development. The Indian
pharmaceutical industry is such that it is investing well and this is the reason why we
were able to develop our own vaccine even in times like Covid. Vishal Sikka, who
is the former CEO of Infosys, during his tenure, Infosys had donated $1 billion to Open AI in 2015 itself.
Vishal Sikka had realized its potential in 2015 itself
and he wanted to integrate it into Infosys in the future. The company
could have been taken much further but he was fired by the board members in 2017 itself.
After this, Vishal Sikka also went to the US like others and
started a company named Viaan AI there, which has received funding of Rs 140 million and this project
looks quite promising. The culture of India has become such that people having out-of-the-box
thinking have to achieve something extraordinary as soon as they go out.
The rest is that when I was studying this whole PhD thing, I
got a very interesting perspective. In India, doing PhD in Maths or Physics
is considered a job for very rare people. Generally no one wants to do it, but all the
people want to do B.Tech in CSIT because after that they get software jobs.
Look now but what is happening, the tables have turned completely, all
the LLMs are being made, Chat GPT Deep Seek, as many people are being employed here. He has done
PhD in Mathematics and Physics etc. and the model he
is making with AI is eating away the jobs of all those software engineers who
had come after doing B.Tech in CSIT, so the tables have been completely turned. If
I talk about conclusion, then to develop the culture of research and development, there
is a need to do course correction at many levels here. This
will start from the government only. Now the government is also taking some initiatives. In 2023 itself, the government
had established the National Research Foundation and in this budget,
funds have also been given for research and development in deep tech. Recently, the government has
started giving free subscription
to many portals or researches published through One Nation One Subscription, so that
it becomes a little easier for those who want to do research. I make
many research papers in it and I have to read them myself. I myself feel that
if people do not do PhD then no one will write the research paper, otherwise
where will I get the data, hence it is very important to do research and go for PhD, but we
are still investing very little in Research and Development. The government
should spend at least 2% of the GDP in Research and Development. Apart from this, the government
will have to encourage the private sector as well or will have to beat a little baton that brother
research. Invest money in etc. The government can also bring such a policy that the company which
invests a certain percentage of its profit in research will
be given some exemption in tax and in this way they can be incentivized. Apart from this,
the government should ensure that there is no reduction in the research funding within the universities.
If there is no infrastructure, children
will not get equipment, then what is the point of going to research courses and
if these universities do not have their own infrastructure. If we develop and collaborate with the industry,
then the children will also be happy and the industry will also be happy that they
will get the availability of such a good talent pool in India and perhaps
we will be able to stop the brain
drain that happens on a large level in the US, UK and outside countries.
